# Abstract {.unnumbered}

We present Cortext, a local multimodal memory engine that stores and recalls
long conversational and sensory streams without calling a language model on
either path.

*Write path.* An online Bayesian change-point segmenter over embedding
statistics closes each source stream into coherent units, and every closed
unit is stored. A stored unit is indexed at three granularities: a pooled unit
vector, one shared-space vector per member signal, and 16 int8
late-interaction codes per text or image payload, up to 16. Its text also
enters an FTS5 keyword index.

*Read path.* A query builds a dense seed list over pooled unit vectors, into
which best-member hits are merged. When auxiliary channels return hits, it
fuses that list by reciprocal-rank fusion with BM25 keyword seeds, one
gap-corrected list per other stored modality, and an optional reference-time
list. A 0.1M-parameter
late-interaction MaxSim reranker over frozen AIST-87M position features then
reorders the top 64. Hydration attaches adjacent turns, superseded
predecessors and superseding successors, each with its own timestamp, and fits
the packet to a caller-supplied byte budget.

*Results.* Under one shared answer model, judge and 34,800-byte budget on
LoCoMo, Cortext scores 86.2%, against 89.0% for Mem0 and 81.0% for Graphiti.
It makes zero write-time model calls and recalls in 9.7 ms at the median.

*Negative result.* A leave-one-out ablation on evaluations of up to 111k turns
tested the bio-inspired lifecycle mechanisms of earlier versions: strength
decay and eviction, reconsolidation, clustering consolidation,
retrieval-induced forgetting, synaptic tagging and neuromodulation. Each was
inert at its defaults or hurt recall once it fired. Eviction alone cut packet
recall from 0.630 to 0.086. We report which benchmarks overlap the reranker's
training data. The original three-knob control design (Focus, Sensitivity,
Stability) remains as a macro-control surface over a calibrated default
profile.

**Keywords:** long-term memory, event segmentation, hybrid retrieval,
reciprocal-rank fusion, late interaction, multimodal retrieval, negative
results

# Introduction

An assistant that runs for months accumulates more history than any context
window holds. The common answer is to spend language-model calls at write
time: extract facts, summarize sessions, maintain a knowledge graph, and
retrieve from those products later [@packer2023memgpt; @chhikara2025mem0;
@rasmussen2025zep]. This works, but it makes memory as expensive and as slow
as the model. It rewrites what was said into what a model inferred, and it
cannot run on a device without one.

Cortext takes the other path. It stores what was observed, as segmented
units of the original signals, and puts the work into retrieval and
hydration. Neither path calls a language model. The only learned components
are a frozen multimodal encoder (AIST-87M) and a 0.1M-parameter
late-interaction reranker over its per-position features.

This paper is a rewrite of the earlier Cortext specification, which presented
a three-knob (F, S, T) cognitive architecture: twelve metrics blended by
recursive least squares, mood and affect, a homeostatic write threshold, and a
family of bio-inspired lifecycle mechanisms. Long-horizon ablation showed the
lifecycle mechanisms did not earn their place (@sec-negative), and removing
the write threshold raised recall. What drives recall in the current (v5)
engine is a different set of mechanisms. The paper is organized around them.

The contributions are:

1. **LLM-free online segmentation, storing every closed unit**
   (@sec-thresholding). A calibrated change-point posterior over surprisal,
   drift, coherence, topic shift and inter-arrival gaps decides unit
   boundaries per source stream. The write rule is
   `write_memory = force_write ∨ should_flush`.
2. **Multi-granularity hybrid retrieval** (@sec-retrieval). Dense seeds
   score pooled unit vectors, and best-member hits raise or join them in the
   same list. Reciprocal-rank fusion (k = 60) then combines that list with
   FTS5 BM25, one z-gated list per other stored modality, and a
   reference-time list, whenever any of those returns hits.
3. **A modality-agnostic late-interaction reranker** (@sec-retrieval). Each
   stored member keeps up to 16 int8 spherical k-means codes of its encoder
   positions, at most about 1 KB. Queries rerank the top 64 by gated MaxSim with a
   learned first-stage rank prior, in 0.4 to 3 ms.
4. **Hydration and evidence fitting** (@sec-hydration):
   * contiguity with adjacent turns;
   * superseded-predecessor and superseding-successor attachment through
     `supersedes` edges;
   * standing directives outside the ranked list;
   * per-blob content timestamps;
   * a per-call evidence budget that trims grouped units to their best
     members before dropping whole memories.
5. **Negative results** (@sec-negative). A leave-one-out study removed:
   * forgetting through strength decay and eviction;
   * reconsolidation;
   * clustering consolidation;
   * retrieval-induced forgetting;
   * synaptic tagging;
   * the NE-like and DA-like neuromodulators;
   * meta-learned priors and several feedback loops.

   It also found that short-horizon blind-judge screens had reported harm
   from removing mechanisms whose packets were byte-identical.
6. **Realtime systems design** (@sec-optimization):
   * a content-addressed embedding arena;
   * a sparse in-memory route;
   * off-thread WAL checkpointing;
   * sound family-collapse bounds;
   * a top-k BM25 collector.

   Together these keep query p95 at 44.5 ms on a 443k-turn store.

@sec-overview gives the whole pipeline and says exactly what the three knobs
still influence. @sec-math fixes notation and the knob maps. Then come
segmentation and the write path (@sec-thresholding), retrieval
(@sec-retrieval) and hydration (@sec-hydration), which form the main line.
The per-signal control stack follows (@sec-core-adaptation,
@sec-structural-metrics), with working memory and supersession
(@sec-advanced), the streaming interrupt gate (@sec-interrupt), maintenance
(@sec-consolidation), and the record of removed reinforcement and decay
(@sec-reinforcement). @sec-negative presents the ablation, @sec-experimental
the full experimental record with reranker-overlap separation,
@sec-implementation implementation detail, and @sec-optimization the systems
architecture. The historical optimization ledger is preserved in
Appendix E (`docs/paper/appendix/optimization_ledger.qmd`).

# Related Work

## LLM Memory Systems and Benchmarks

MemGPT [@packer2023memgpt] pages context in and out of a model's window under
model control. Mem0 [@chhikara2025mem0] extracts and consolidates facts with
a model at write time, and Zep [@rasmussen2025zep] (with its open-source
engine Graphiti) maintains a temporal knowledge graph built by model calls.
Cortext differs in kind: it makes no model call on either path, and it stores
observed signals rather than model-written facts. @sec-v5-benchmarks
compares it with Mem0 and Graphiti under one shared pipeline on LoCoMo
[@maharana2024locomo], and with published results on LongMemEval
[@wu2024longmemeval], BEAM, DolphinBench and MemLens.

## Event Segmentation

Cortext's unit of memory comes from event segmentation theory
[@zacks2007event]: people segment continuous experience at points of
prediction error, and those boundaries structure later recall. EM-LLM
[@fountas2024em] segments token streams into episodic events by surprise,
refined by graph-theoretic cohesion. Cortext adapts the idea to any embedding
stream. EMA prediction error supplies surprise, within-unit cosine coherence
supplies cohesion, and drift, topic shift and inter-arrival gaps supply
further evidence for a calibrated change-point posterior
(@sec-thresholding). Because it operates on embeddings, the same segmenter
serves text turns, audio chunks and images.

## Hybrid and Late-Interaction Retrieval

BM25 [@robertson2009probabilistic] remains a strong lexical baseline, and
fusing lexical and dense rankings by reciprocal rank [@cormack2009reciprocal]
is a robust, training-free way to combine them. Cortext uses RRF with the
standard k = 60 over the dense list (with member hits merged in), the
keyword list, the per-modality cross-modal lists and the temporal list. Late-interaction retrieval
[@khattab2020colbert] scores a query against a document's per-token vectors
by MaxSim. Cortext applies it as a reranker over frozen encoder positions of
any modality. Each stored member compresses its positions to at most 16 int8
spherical k-means codes, which keeps storage near 1 KB per payload without a
shared codebook. The sparse candidate route follows the HNSW construction
[@malkov2018efficient].

## Working Memory Models

The working memory component draws conceptually on @cowan2001magical
embedded-processes model, which posits a capacity limit of about 4±1 chunks
for the focus of attention. That figure contrasts with @miller1956magical
earlier estimate of 7±2 items, which later research showed conflates chunking
with raw capacity [@cowan2010magical]. Cortext's production slots are larger
application-level memory units rather than cognitive chunks. The shipped
F/S-derived capacity is 15–27 slots, 21 at neutral knobs, selected from the
product evaluation in @sec-experimental. The biological result motivates a
bounded set, not a claim that the software reproduces human span. The
episodic buffer of @baddeley2000episodic aligns with binding information
across modalities through one shared vector space.

## Consolidation, Reconsolidation and Forgetting

Complementary learning systems [@mcclelland1995why] motivate a fast episodic
store beside slower structure, and reconsolidation theory
[@nader2000fear; @nader2003memory] holds that retrieved memories become
labile and can be modified before restabilizing. Earlier Cortext versions
implemented the following, each with knob-derived rates:

* reconsolidation drift during a lability window;
* clustering consolidation into abstraction nodes;
* multi-timescale strength decay with eviction;
* retrieval-induced forgetting [@anderson1994remembering].

All four were evaluated and removed (@sec-negative). Reconsolidation was
neutral to harmful, and consolidation never fired at its defaults and did not
help when forced. Eviction deleted 92–99.7% of stores once its gate opened.
The engine now keeps the episodic substrate [@tulving1972episodic] and no
consolidated semantic tier. Its only consolidation-like step is maintenance
of the retrieval route (@sec-consolidation).

## Emotional Influences on Memory

@mcgaugh2004amygdala showed that arousal modulates memory consolidation
through amygdala-mediated effects on hippocampal encoding
[@labar2006cognitive]. Earlier Cortext versions implemented emotional
consolidation and an emotional cascade over graph neighbours. Both were
removed after leaving every packet byte-identical (@sec-negative). The
per-signal emotion projection onto a dimensional valence-arousal model
[@russell1980circumplex] remains in the control stack. Its valence and
arousal feed the composite score and the streaming interrupt gate
(@sec-core-adaptation). The emotion threshold delta and the mood integrator
were removed with the dynamic threshold.

## Adaptive Control

Earlier versions steered a write threshold with a homeostatic controller,
following proportional-integral setpoint control [@astrom2008feedback], with
an effective-sample-size reliability estimate from sequential Monte Carlo
[@liu1998sequential]. Once every closed unit was stored, the controller had
no consumer, and it was removed (@sec-spike-threshold). The adaptive pieces
that remain are EWMA rate and cadence estimates, an uncertainty estimate that
sets learning rates, and recursive-least-squares blending of the composite
score (@sec-structural-metrics).

# Conclusion and Future Directions

Cortext stores what it observed and puts its effort into retrieval. Online
segmentation decides what a memory is, and every closed unit is kept.
Retrieval works at three granularities over unit vectors, member vectors and
late-interaction codes, and fuses dense, keyword, cross-modal and temporal
evidence by reciprocal rank. A 0.1M-parameter reranker over a frozen encoder
reorders the head of the pool. Hydration then rebuilds the context around
each hit and fits it to the reader's budget. With no language model on
either path, this reaches 86.2% on LoCoMo under a shared pipeline, 2.8 points
behind a system that spends 544 model calls at write time, with recall about
17× faster.

The negative result matters as much as the system. The bio-inspired
lifecycle mechanisms that earlier versions of this paper put at the centre
did not survive long-horizon ablation. Short-horizon judged screens had also
attributed effects to mechanisms whose packets never changed. We recommend
two practices to memory-system work: diff packets before judging, and ablate
on the engine that ships.

Future work:

1. **A measured forgetting policy.** The store grows without bound. Any
   tiering or eviction must first be gated on packet recall over month-scale
   timestamps.
2. **Out-of-pool gold.** At BEAM 1M and 10M, 42% and 67% of gold turns never
   enter the candidate pool. This, not reranking, is the next recall lever.
3. **Reranker coverage.** The reranker needs an audio position map and
   re-encoding of stored codes when the reranker model changes.
4. **Zero-shot evaluation.** The reranker should be evaluated on more
   benchmarks it was never trained on.
5. **Standing-directive detection.** The current detector is a pattern
   check, and a learned one could replace it.
